subject: Prompt eval governance — action & rollback triggers
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt eval governance — action & rollback triggers

Rishi, team — quick heads up from product: the latest canary for the prompt suite shipped to Acme (canary-id: c-20270408) is showing a small but consistent drop in helpfulness for the finance cohort. Numbers below; full exports attached.

- Delta in helpfulness (human-rated): -5.9% relative to baseline
- Regression concentrated on prompts with long-context ( > 1.5k tokens)
- No clear uptick in hallucination rate but lower answer completeness on multi-step queries

Ask: can we hold the wider rollout until we agree on acceptance criteria and a mitigation path? Specific asks below:

1) Define an immediate rollback/hold trigger (what threshold and which metric).
2) Recommend a temporary fallback variant (smaller model / quantized variant) we can route to for the finance cohort.
3) Owners for a fast triage run (who runs the short A/B with labeled prompts, timeline 24h).

I realize this will touch infra and evals — looping in Jonas and Marissa for triage and orchestration. Acme is sensitive because this is an internal tool for their FP&A. I suggest a quick sync in 2 hours.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Product Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: eval_summary_v2.csv, metric_broken_down_by_cohort.csv

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt eval governance — action & rollback triggers

Thanks Laura — I agree we should pause. Quick clarifying questions before the sync:

- Which metric should be authoritative for the hold? Human helpfulness score or a proxy (e.g., accepted answer rate)?
- Do we have per-prompt labels for the finance cohort to run a focused A/B (20–50 prompts)?

Proposed immediate plan (24h window):
1) Hold rollout (set routing rule to keep 100% on existing prod variant for affected tenant cohort). I can push the routing change if we sign off.
2) Jonas to run a focused A/B on the flagged prompt list with the previous model variant and the new one (N=50).
3) Marissa to notify Acme SRE/PM and offer a short remediation timeline + status update.

I'll be on the sync in ~15. If we want rollback thresholds, I propose: helpfulness drop > 4% AND at least 10 labeled prompts affected => trigger hold. Open to adjustments.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt eval governance — action & rollback triggers

Short technical notes from the eval side (ran preliminary scripts attached):

- I ran the cohort split and verified the -5.9% helpfulness across 320 sampled sessions; when we restrict to the curated 50-prompt finance set, the drop is -6.4% (p=0.03).
- Cohort skew: effect concentrated in prompts with > 1.5k tokens and where the prompt includes a tabular paste.
- No significant change in model confidence distribution; suggests model is returning shorter / incomplete steps rather than more hallucinations.

Suggested immediate acceptance criteria for rollback/hold: any of the following should trigger a hold:
- Helpful score delta <= -4.0% on the curated prompt set (N >= 30)
- Net NPS/acceptance proxy delta <= -3% for the cohort in a 24h window
- Any catastrophic failure flagged by production monitors (latency/error excursions)

Suggested temporary fallback: route finance cohort to prod-variant-v1.8 (previous trained checkpoint) for 48–72h while we triage. That variant has comparable latency/cost and matches baseline helpfulness in internal tests.

Attachments: canary_log_20270410.txt

I'll run the 50-prompt A/B and upload the labeled annotation CSV by EOD. If we want a stricter policy, we can add a secondary check on answer completeness (>= 85% required).

- Jonas
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: sara.lopez@acme-corp.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: acme-ml-eng@example.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt eval governance — action & rollback triggers

Thanks for the quick flag. From Acme's side: this cohort is used in monthly close flows — a small drop in helpfulness has outsized business impact. We prefer a conservative approach (hold + fallback). Please keep us updated; we can fast-track annotated examples from our team if that helps.

Sara Lopez
Product Manager, Acme Corp
sara.lopez@acme-corp.com

Summary and owners / next steps (per today's sync):

1) Rollout hold: Approved. Rishi will update routing to pin finance cohort to prod-variant-v1.8 within the hour. (Owner: Rishi — target +1h)
2) Focused A/B: Jonas to run 50-prompt labeled comparison and share annotated CSV + basic stats (helpfulness, completeness) by EOD. (Owner: Jonas — target EOD)
3) Acceptance criteria formalized: Helpful delta <= -4% on curated set OR completeness < 85% => keep hold. We also require N >= 30.
4) Customer comms: Marissa to send status update to Acme and schedule a 30-minute follow-up Friday at 4:30pm PT. (Owner: Marissa — in flight)
5) Remediation runway: If A/B confirms regression, product and applied ML will propose a patch/rollforward plan by Monday morning with QA signoff.

I'll create a short Decision Log in Drive and link JIRA ticket INF-8421 for tracking.

Thanks everyone — this was a good quick cross-functional response.

Marissa Cole
